Class StackAdapter

java.lang.Object
myAdapter.StackAdapter
All Implemented Interfaces:
HCollection, HList
public class StackAdapter extends Object implements HList
Stack adapter that implements the HList interface, providing a LIFO data structure backed by a java.util.Vector of CLDC 1.1 (Adapter pattern: the Vector is the adaptee). This implementation supports null elements and elements of any type, and follows the behavior of java.util.Stack and of the J2SE 1.4.2 Collections Framework.

Mapping between the stack and the list view: the element at index 0 is the bottom of the stack and the element at index size() - 1 is the top. push() appends at the end, pop() and peek() work on the last element, and the iterators traverse the elements from the bottom (index 0) to the top.

    • search

      public int search(Object o)
      Returns the 1-based position where an object is on this stack. If the object o occurs as an item in this stack, this method returns the distance from the top of the stack of the occurrence nearest the top of the stack; the topmost item on the stack is considered to be at distance 1. The equals method is used to compare o to the items in this stack.
      Parameters:
      o - the desired object.
      Returns:
      the 1-based position from the top of the stack where the object is located; the return value -1 indicates that the object is not on the stack.

    • toArray

      public Object[] toArray()
      Returns an array containing all of the elements in this HCollection in proper sequence. The returned array will be "safe" in that no references to it are maintained by this HCollection. (In other words, this method must allocate a new array even if this HCollection is backed by an array). The caller is thus free to modify the returned array.
      Specified by:
      toArray in interface HCollection
      Returns:
      an array containing all of the elements in this HCollection.

    • toArray

      public Object[] toArray(Object[] a)
      Returns an array containing all of the elements in this HCollection, from the bottom to the top of the stack. If the HCollection fits in the specified array, it is stored and returned therein; if the array has more elements than this HCollection, the element immediately following the last one is set to null. Otherwise, a new array with the size of this HCollection is allocated and returned. Since CLDC 1.1 does not provide java.lang.reflect.Array, the new array cannot have the runtime type of the specified array: it is always an Object[].
      Specified by:
      toArray in interface HCollection
      Parameters:
      a - the array into which the elements of this HCollection are to be stored, if it is big enough.
      Returns:
      an array containing the elements of this HCollection.
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if the specified array is null.
      ArrayStoreException - if the runtime type of the specified array is not a supertype of the runtime type of every element in this HCollection.

    • equals

      public boolean equals(Object o)
      Compares the specified object with this HCollection for equality. Returns true if and only if the specified object is also an HList, both lists have the same size, and all corresponding pairs of elements are equal (two elements e1 and e2 are equal if (e1==null ? e2==null : e1.equals(e2))). In other words, two lists are equal if they contain the same elements in the same order.

      public boolean addAll(int index, HCollection c)
      Inserts all of the elements in the specified HCollection into this HList at the specified position.     • subList

      public HList subList(int fromIndex, int toIndex)
      Returns a view of the portion of this HList between the specified fromIndex, inclusive, and toIndex, exclusive. (If fromIndex and toIndex are equal, the returned HList is empty.) The returned HList is backed by this HList, so changes in the returned HList (including structural ones such as add, remove and clear) are reflected in this HList, and non-structural changes in this HList are reflected in the returned HList. The returned HList supports all of the optional list operations supported by this HList. If this HList is structurally modified in any way other than via the returned HList, the behavior of the returned HList is undefined.
      Specified by:
      subList in interface HList
      Parameters:
      fromIndex - low endpoint (inclusive) of the subList.
      toIndex - high endpoint (exclusive) of the subList.
      Returns:
      a view of the specified range within this HList.
      Throws:
      IndexOutOfBoundsException - for an illegal endpoint index value (fromIndex < 0 || toIndex > size || fromIndex > toIndex).
